successors.name: Federated Republic of Mexico
successors.text: the core of Mexico without the Yucatán peninsula, returned when the Constitution of 1824 was restored on 22 August 1846

ledger.x: 1835: the federal constitution is repealed and the Centralist Republic begins.
1840: the federalists of Yucatán rise against the centralists.

1840: Yucatán is lost to the federalist rebels, who declare independence on 16 March 1841 ('a crowd led by Miguel Barbachano Terrazo ... broke into the room calling for the independence of Yucatán'; infobox 'Independence March 16 1841').
1842: Cliopatria's Centralist shape grows from 4,886 to 7,186 cells; 1,266 of them are Chihuahua, Durango and a corner of New Mexico taken from the Federated row.
1842: the three states of the Rio Grande rising of 1840 are back in the Centralist shape.
1843: the campaign ends in a settlement.
1846: the federal constitution is restored and the Centralist Republic ends.

wars.name: Texas Revolution
wars.outcome: Texas won de facto independence; Mexico did not recognise it: on 29 July 1836 the government 'issued a manifesto disavowing Santa Anna's recognition of Texan independence'.

wars.name: Pastry War
wars.outcome: French victory without territorial change: French naval forces blockaded the Gulf ports from 27 November 1838 and 'withdrew on 9 March 1839 after a peace treaty was signed'; Mexico paid damages.

wars.name: Yucatán federalist revolt and war of independence
wars.outcome: The federalists took Campeche (6 June 1840) and declared independence (16 March 1841); a Mexican naval force took Carmen Island in August 1842; Santa Anna conceded autonomy on 5 December 1843 and the republic 'retained its sovereignty'.

wars.name: Mexican-American War

certainty.note: No pages opened date a treaty line for the northern frontier; the Texas boundary and the Soconusco were disputed (Guatemala claimed the Soconusco until Mexico took it in 1842), and Yucatán was in revolt from 1840.
